summary.intent: Win the Lio 'Keep the Line Running' hackathon challenge for Soony: analyze the confidential supply-chain data drops, then build and ship an agent-based product that rechecks the launch plan, flags contradictions, and acts (supplier emails, approvals, phone calls) before the Sunday 12:00 hand-in.
summary.outcome: Found that the launch plan's 'all ok' hid real shortfalls (overbooked art book receipt, failed statue lot, rev B/C sleeve conflict, card shortage). Built a Python poller plus agent product with a Today/Launch web UI, phone sign-off flow, a dry-mail demo instance, a phone-to-case bridge, README and demo script; all 335 tests pass. Work is on branch jonas/today-flow, with the latest commits not yet pushed and a real test call to the user's phone still in progress.

repo: Portal API has only three endpoints (files list, single file, archive.zip) and no webhooks. Change detection must poll and compare SHA-256, since files get replaced under the same name.
Confidential portal data lives in the gitignored data/ folder; .env holds the token, .env.example is committed. Never put data values in code or commit them.
The repo uses a team workflow (CLAUDE.md, PROGRESS.md) where tasks are claimed in PROGRESS.md; Entire hooks checkpoint on commit and push checkpoints with git push.
Entire skips checkpoints when no repo files changed, so a session of read-only analysis shows no checkpoint.

Two server instances run behind a Cloudflare tunnel: live (:8000) and demo (:8001, ask-soony-demo.stenglein.dev). The demo is controlled through scripts/demo.sh (reset, snapshot, stop, CALLS=twilio) and sends supplier mail dry only.
The frontend polls state every 5 seconds (POLL_MS=5000) in App.tsx, so phone or push decisions show up on both Today and Launch within about 5s.
Push notifications go to every subscribed device, not per person. Sign-off names are matched by first-name heuristic.

Calls default to ASK_CALL_PROVIDER=dry_run; real Twilio calls cost about $0.38/min. The phone bridge (card_alerts.py) is off on live via ASK_CARD_ALERTS=off, and the alert DB is shared between live and demo, so links are stored per state folder.
The CSV readers in the paper check and the team's verifier were UTF-8-only; they needed encoding fallbacks and handling of rows with more fields than the header.

code.finding: One-time /ok/<token> approval links (valid until launch) let an approver Approve or Decline on a phone without a password. Approve executes the option at most once through the normal email, duplicate-check and money-rule path.

Bridges cases to phone alerts: raises one alert per red or soon-due untouched case (max 1 open), and applies phone decisions to the case exactly once. Cases awaiting sign-off are routed to the signer instead of being executed.

build_state assembles the case trail including phone and sign-off lines. The shared mailbox sync had a lost-update race in the outbox action log, fixed by appending under the shared lock (commit dd71984).

J/K navigation must step by grouped list rows, not by individual cards, or folded groups (e.g. '5 like this') lose their highlight. Cmd+Enter triggers the primary button; option key badges appear only after keyboard use.

workflow: Delegating long parallel jobs (cross-checking 200 order confirmations and 59 scans, building the sign-off loop and phone bridge) to subagents while writing README and docs in the main thread worked well.
Rehearsing the demo script end to end on the demo instance surfaced real bugs, such as a truncated sentence on rev B cases.
A scheduled external action (a Cloudflare DNS route) was first pointed at the wrong tunnel, causing the Error 1033 the user saw; verify the tunnel binding right after creating routes.
Costly or external actions (real calls, supplier emails, pushes) were gated by asking the user first, and the demo ran dry by default.

friction: The Cloudflare Tunnel Error 1033 on the demo host came from the DNS record pointing at the wrong tunnel for a minute.
A lost-update race in the mailbox sync wiped the record of the 07:58 Karton approval; the email itself had gone out and the record had to be restored from the Sent folder.
The J/K highlight disappeared and the order seemed to jump on folded rows.

The UI had several contradictory or odd bits: a switched-off routine said 'Watching', the 'Handled 3 cases' line had only a small clickable 'show', and the status sentence 'Your agents are on it' was vague.
Safari caches favicons stubbornly, so the old yellow icon may persist.
The user had to ask repeatedly whether things were pushed; commits piled up locally (up to 8).
Push notifications cannot target a specific person, so the 'Maren's phone' demo depends on which device is subscribed.
The first real Twilio test call was started but its outcome was not confirmed within the transcript, and CSV encoding problems in the new drop interrupted it.
